title: Sound engine, music and room music
divergences: Not compared with hardware or an emulator. MidiKey2Freq (BIOS) uses the high-level formula; the PSG and the output mixer are an emulation of the GBA sound hardware, resampled to 48 kHz with a zero-order hold of the FIFO; REG_VCOUNT reads as 160 during UpdateAudio. The runtime has no door transition, so the room's track starts 32 frames after the fade begins; the alarm, Norfair and cutscene music cases (unk_378c, unk_38d8, the gMusicTrackInfo.unk checks) and the volume down of gUnk_Audio0x50 (unk_3058 in ReplayQueuedMusic) are not ported. The 7-entry channel backups drop what would overflow them instead of writing past the array. A zero divisor in unk_1ccc is taken as a zero quotient.
notes: The custom C engine is ported routine by routine with the assembly mixer: the sequencer commands, DirectSound channels with the native envelope, allocation and group-of-four mixing paths, the four PSG channels through their registers, reverb, fades and the sound queue. ROM data (songs, voice groups, samples) is read through its GBA addresses from a private sound bank; out-of-table ROM reads of GetNoteDelay and unk_1ccc are exported. Rooms export their musicTrack and the runtime plays it through CheckSetNewMusicTrack and CheckPlayTransitionMusicTrack; the gameplay modules request their sound effects through mzm_sfx (identifiers generated from the decompilation's Sound enum by scripts/mzm_sound_ids.py), which the runtime forwards to the engine. InsertMusicAndQueueCurrent saves the channels of players 1, 3, 6 and 8 (unk_34ac), stops the others and plays the inserted music on player 0; its 0xB6 end runs ReplayQueuedMusic, which restores them (unk_35d0) and restarts the current music. BackupTrackData2SoundChannels / RetrieveTrackData2SoundChannels release and restore the channels of player 2; mzm_sfx carries PlayMusic, the insertion and the backup requests. With the extracted bank the item jingle plays 355 frames before Brinstar resumes (an engine-only check: captures have no sound).
next_action: Trigger the sounds of the systems still to port (charge beam, bombs, liquids, ground effects, bosses); compare a rendered track with an emulator capture.

notes: The eight item statues (Long, Ice and Wave Beams, Bombs, Speed Booster, High Jump, Screw Attack, Varia Suit) and their hint statues run ChozoStatue with gSubSpriteData1: the multi-sprite tables (Standing, Sitting, Seated) are read from the decompilation, the head and leg take their OAM and position from it, the eye, arm and glow parts their position; the statue faces its native direction, makes its seated or standing body solid (CAA_MAKE_NON_POWER_GRIP, the hint statue's hand CAA_MAKE_SOLID_GRIPPABLE) and spawns its parts and, while Samus lacks the item, the ball. The ball (SSC_SOLID, one health) reveals the item when shot, then Samus touching it starts gPreventMovementTimer, registers the item and its events (ChozoStatueRegisterItem) and opens the item's one-line message banner, the ball flickering until the banner closes; the statue then waits 40 frames and idles, its arm glowing. Statues draw with their own graphics; the sprite engine gained drawOrder, SP_ALWAYS_ACTIVE and graphics owners for secondary sprites. Checked in brinstar_005: shooting the ball reveals the Long Beam orb, touching it shows the "Long Beam" banner, and after A the ball is gone and the hand glows. The statue's hand grabs Samus (SPOSE_GRABBED_BY_CHOZO_STATUE, at its exact height and within a quarter block): a hint statue in the Morph Ball or rolling registers the hint, opens its eye, flashes its palette rows (sChozoStatueFlashingPaletteRows every 12 frames, the hint sound), sits down along the Sitting table with flickering echoes (SpawnChozoStatueMovement), seats and refills; a refill statue in the Morph Ball refills energy, missiles, super missiles and power bombs (SpriteUtilRefill*, each followed by 13 frames of its HUD counter) with the refill glow and palette flash, opens "Energy Tank recharge complete" or "Weapons and energy fully restored", sleeps, closes its eye and lets Samus go when she may move. The exporter adds the statues' palette rows 1 to 3. Checked in brinstar_005 (`--spawn 126 112 --item long-beam`, Down twice): grabbed, golden flash, refill banner, released in the hand; in brinstar_002 (`--spawn 808 112`, Down twice) the Long Beam hint statue grabs Samus, flashes, sits down with her and refills. The unknown item statues (Plasma Beam, Space Jump, Gravity Suit) run the same AI with their own OAM tables (UnknownItemChozoStatue*, the unknown balls), multi-sprite tables (read from the positional initializers of the decompilation), part and refill sprites; their item is obtained (gEquipment.beamBombs / suitMisc) but stays inactive, as UpdateSuitType keeps it for the normal suit, and its banner reads "Unknown Item". Checked in kraid_033 (`--spawn 186 128`, B, Right): the Space Jump statue's ball reveals the unknown orb and touching it shows "Unknown Item".

title: Doors, hatches and room transitions
divergences: Door fades, the hatch locks (gDoorUnlockTimer, events) and their unlocking (with its sound) and the mother ship hatch graphics are not reproduced; opened destinations are remembered by position, not by door index.
notes: Hatches are BG1 and Clipdata blocks driven by the native state machine: BgClipCheckOpeningHatch on beam, missile and laser hits (weakness and health from sHatchBehaviors, super missiles open missile hatches), the opening and closing frames of sHatchesTilemapValues with sHatchesAnimationDurationCounter, the hatch Samus comes through closing behind her, opened hatches remembered per area and overridden to normal hatches. Checked in brinstar_000: a beam opens the blue hatch through its grey frames.
next_action: Port the door fades and the hatch locks with their events.

title: Beam and missile projectiles
divergences: The on-screen test of ProjectileCheckDespawn uses the runtime camera's top-left corner with the GBA screen size (the runtime view is wider); the missile trails' low BG priority is not drawn; projectiles without PROJ_STATUS_ABOVE_BG1 are drawn at the sprites' priority instead of one behind BG1.
notes: Power Beam, missiles and super missiles move and collide with the room; their hits on ported sprites (damage, stun, invincible hits) and their wall and sprite impact particles are ported. Missiles and super missiles drop their trails (PE_MISSILE_TRAIL every 8 frames, PE_SUPER_MISSILE_TRAIL every 4). ProjectileCheckDespawn removes beams and missiles that are both off screen (the screen plus the projectile's draw distance and two blocks of padding) and 12 blocks above or below or 10 blocks beside Samus. A missile or super missile not weak to the sprite it hits (or hitting an immune sprite) tumbles off it (ProjectileStartTumblingMissile: away from the sprite's x, its thrust sound stopped, no longer hitting sprites, drawn in front of the backgrounds) along sTumblingMissileSpeed with a pixel a frame sideways and through walls, until it leaves the screen (ProjectileMoveTumbling). Checked in brinstar_003: a missile shot diagonally at a brown Ripper bounces back and falls tumbling. (The charge and Long Beams: mzm.weapons.charge_beam; Ice: mzm.weapons.ice_beam; Wave and Plasma: mzm.weapons.wave_plasma_beams; bombs and power bombs: mzm.weapons.bombs, mzm.weapons.power_bombs). The weapon sounds play at their native points: the toggle and arming sounds of SamusSetHighlightedWeapon, the beam shot and the missile and super missile shot and thrust on ProjectileInit, the thrust stopped by the impact particles.
next_action: Add the missile and beam item pickups with the item sprites.

title: Bombs, bomb jumps and bomb damage
divergences: The morph ball launcher stages and liquids (no bounce when slowed) are not ported; the sprite pass of the explosion runs after the projectile loop in the runtime, so the bomb keeps a flag for the frame the native pass (before the loop) sees it.
notes: With the Bombs item, B in the Morph Ball places a bomb (four at most, 7 frames apart) at Samus's position: a slow then a fast spin of 16 frames each with their native sprites, then the PE_BOMB explosion and 16 frames during which CAA_BOMB_PISTOL reaches nine points, one a frame (bomb blocks, bomb chains, hatches). On the first explosion frame Samus bounces off a touching bomb (up, left or right from the bomb's middle and gPreviousXPosition; only falling and from below when airborne), and the explosion damages sprites weak to beams and bombs (8). The set and explosion sounds play. Checked in brinstar_000: the bounce, then the three bomb blocks under Samus break.
next_action: Port the morph ball launchers.

title: Charge Beam, Long Beam and the pseudo screw
divergences: The pseudo screw's Samus effect is not drawn; the suitless pistol is not ported.
notes: With the Charge Beam, holding B with no weapon armed counts the charge to 79, then back to 64; releasing it fires a charged beam from 64 or a normal beam above 25; the B press itself still fires a beam, arming a weapon drops the charge and the Morph Ball releases a full charge as it forms or rolls. The charging particle starts at 16 with the begin-to-charge sound (stopped when the charge drops), turns charged at 64 with the full-charge loop every 16 frames, follows the arm cannon and hides in the spin poses; Samus uses the charging palette rows (two consecutive rows by 16-frame step, none on the fourth) and the beam release rows. The Long Beam moves 24 subpixels a frame without the short lifetime, with its hit damage (3) and impact; the charged beams (two at a time, hitboxes 12 and 16, damage 8 and 12) hit sprites weak to the charge beam or beams. Beam shots set the ProjectileSetBeamParticleEffect flash at the cannon. A full charge during a spin is the pseudo screw: 4 * (2 + beams) to weak sprites, PSEUDO_SCREW_DESTROYED on a kill, Samus still hurt by survivors. The beam particles are exported per loaded beam variant (graphics set and sBeamPal row) in the projectile library. Checked in tourian_010: the charge glow and palette, then the charged Long Beam and its flash. The charged Long Beam drops PE_CHARGED_LONG_BEAM_TRAIL every 8 frames.
next_action: Port the suitless pistol with the suitless Samus.

title: Ice Beam and freezing
divergences: SpriteUtilCheckOnZipline is not checked (no ziplines); the trails' low BG priority is not drawn; frozenPaletteRowOffset is taken as 0 for every sprite; the suitless Space Pirate freeze flicker is not ported.
notes: The Ice Beam (over the Long Beam) moves 26 subpixels a frame and drops a trailing particle half a block from it when gFrameCounter8Bit & 3 is 0 (drifting one subpixel sideways and one pixel down a frame); its shot, charge and impact sounds, beam graphics, sBeamPal row 2, release row 2 and charging rows 4 and 5 are used. Hits: a sprite weak to beams freezes for 240 when freezable and frame8 & its freeze flag (metadata high byte) is 0, taking 3 (4 with Long Beam) as ice damage; otherwise normal damage; freezable but immune sprites freeze with no damage; others take the solid hit. The charged Ice Beam (12, 16 with Long Beam) needs a charge-beam or beam weakness and always freezes freezable sprites. Freezing sets the frozen row (15 - graphics slot), plays SOUND_FREEZING_SPRITE and the freezing particle (drawn every other frame); every ported AI then only counts the timer down every other frame and flickers in its last 45 ticks. The stun timer now flashes the stun row (14 - slot). The exporter bakes /frozen and /stun variants of every sprite frame. Pseudo screw damage counts the Ice Beam. Checked in brinstar_003 (`--item ice-beam`, L held, B taps): a brown Ripper freezes blue under the ice impact and freezing particles, trails follow the shots and Samus flashes the ice release row. Frozen sprites are solid: a falling Samus lands on them (SpriteUtilSamusStandingOnSprite, STANDING_ENEMY), rising into one stops her under it and walking into one stops her at its side; its kill drops her. Checked in ridley_003 (`--item ice-beam --item charge-beam`): a charged shot freezes a Dessgeega, Samus jumps onto it and stands there until it thaws, then takes its contact damage. The charged Ice Beam also drops PE_CHARGED_ICE_BEAM_TRAIL every 8 frames.
next_action: Port the suitless Space Pirate freeze flicker with the suitless Samus.

title: Power bombs and their explosion
divergences: The explosion's look is an approximation drawn over the background layers behind the sprites (the yellow tint and the BLDY 12 darkening outside the native window rows; the layers in front of the sprites are not darkened), not the native palette and blending registers; PowerBombExplosionEnd's blend fade takes one frame; the screen shake is not reproduced; the native GET_CLIP_BLOCK reads past the room's right edge, the port skips those blocks.
notes: In the Morph Ball, R arms power bombs (with ammunition); B (the Bombs item is required, as natively) places one, at most one at a time and none during an explosion: one ammunition (the last disarms them), a slow spin of 54 frames and a fast one of 40, then PowerBombExplosionStart. The semi-minor axis grows by 3 a frame to 159, holds five frames, shrinks back to 4 and ends; while expanding, CAA_POWER_BOMB reaches the hitbox's left and right block columns (even frames) or top and bottom rows (odd frames) from the centre outward, opening power bomb hatches and breaking blocks; every sprite touching the hitbox takes 50 (weak) once per power bomb. The set and explosion sounds play; power bomb drops spawn and refill one. The window rows come from sHaze_PowerBomb_WindowValuesPointers (power_bomb.tsv). Checked in brinstar_000: the explosion and the bomb blocks it breaks.
next_action: Draw the explosion through the native palette and window effects.

title: Wave and Plasma Beams
divergences: The ice-coloured Wave and Plasma projectiles are pre-rendered with sBeamPal row 2 over their graphics set (the /ice library keys); the projectiles' draw order follows PROJ_STATUS_ABOVE_BG1 only (in front of every background, or at the sprites' priority); no item pickup gives the beams yet (debug menu and --item only).
notes: SamusCheckNewProjectile picks plasma, then wave, ice, long for the beam type and the matching shot sound (all 24 normal and charged combinations); the charge sounds and the release (rows 3 and 4) and charging rows (6 and 8) follow ParticlePlayBeginToChargeSound and SamusUpdatePalette. The Wave Beam moves 28 subpixels a frame through walls, applying CAA_BEAM to three points across the wave (one block away, 45 subpixels diagonally) every frame; the Plasma Beam moves 32 and stops at walls (its impact) unless the Wave Beam is equipped, and goes through the sprites it hits. Both drop the ice trail with the Ice Beam; the charged ones drop their trails (wave, plasma, or the full beam trail with Plasma and Wave) every 8 frames. Their hitboxes are the native per-direction boxes (wave, charged wave and their Plasma variants, with the float factors truncated). Hits deal 3 plus one per other beam (charged 12 plus four) with the Wave or Plasma impact, or are ice hits with the full beam particles when the Ice Beam is equipped. The projectile library exports the Wave and Plasma tables, their ice-coloured versions, the new impact and trail particles for each loaded beam variant (the Plasma trails only with the Plasma graphics). Checked in brinstar_003 (`--item wave-beam --item long-beam`): a wave shot crosses the right wall and stays drawn in front of it until it leaves the screen; with `--item plasma-beam` the green shot goes through a Ripper.
next_action: Add the beam item pickups with the item sprites.
